4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 4’s parsing of the wording is exactly on target: the explicit requirement of “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” together with the clause that “the number of such points and line segments matches the dimension” rules out any sampling scheme that permits axis collisions. Once those inadmissible realizations are excluded, the model reduces precisely to the deterministic one-point-per-fixed-axis construction used by Colleagues 2, 3 and 5. The factor \(P_d = d!/d^d\) therefore never enters the volume expectation; we are left with the clean expression \({\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d = 2^{-d}/d!\) and the pairwise-distance average \([1+(d-1)I_2]/(d+1)\).  

The resulting ratios tabulated by Colleague 5 are therefore the only ones consistent with the problem statement:  
\[
R_1=1,\quad R_2\approx0.21244,\quad R_3\approx0.03293,\quad R_4\approx0.00395,\quad R_5\approx0.00038,\dots
\]  
Their sum converges to the three-decimal value 1.250. Colleague 1’s auxiliary uniform index \(I_k\) re-introduces precisely the collisions the wording forbids, and any hybrid that retains a positive fraction of those events necessarily violates the orthogonality constraint. The conventional cross-polytope normalisation is consequently the sole reading that respects both the geometric language and the uniformity process described in the query.

3.text:
The admissible realisations are those with a distinct point on each of the
$d$ distinct orthogonal axes. With the conventional one point per fixed
axis normalisation

$$
{\cal S}_{d}=\{0,P_{1},\dots ,P_{d}\},\qquad 
P_{i}=U_{i}e_{i},\;\;U_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}{\rm U}(-1,1),
$$

a.s.

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}{\cal S}_{d}\bigr)=\frac{|U_{1}\cdots U_{d}|}{d!},
\qquad 
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{{\mathbb E}|U|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
$$

and ${\mathbb E}\|0-P_{i}\|=1/2$.  For $i\ne j$

$$
d_{0}:={\mathbb E}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
      ={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}\approx0.765195716 .
$$

On the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of ${\cal S}_{d}$

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 d_{0}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)d_{0}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

so that with the $E{\rm Vol}/E{\rm dist}$ normalisation

$$
R_{d}^{0}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
       =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)d_{0}},\qquad R_{1}^{0}=1,
$$

$$
R_{2}^{0}= \frac{3}{4\cdot2!}\frac1{1+d_{0}}\approx0.21244,
\;R_{3}^{0}\approx0.03293,
\;R_{4}^{0}\approx0.00395,
\;R_{5}^{0}\approx3.85\times10^{-4},\dots
$$

$R_{d}^{0}=O\!\left(2^{-d}/d!\right)$.  Hence

$$
S_{\infty}^{0}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.2497,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}^{0}\approx1.250$ on three figures.  The $d=1,2$ terms
essentially exhaust the series; the $d_{0}$-normalised series is
$\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/(d!d_{0})=(e^{1/2}-1)/d_{0}\approx0.848$.

This is the distinct-segment, non-colliding one-point-per-axis
cross-polytope reading required by “$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal
open line segments’’ and “the number of points and line segments
matching the dimension’’.  The $d!/d^{d}$ permutation factor
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\rm iid}=(2d)^{-d}$ of the literal
i.i.d. $X_{k}=R_{k}e_{I_{k}}$ uniform-on-$L_{d}$ model is precisely the
zero-volume collision probability that the distinctness condition
removes.  With that literal i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union convention one
obtains $R_{d}^{\rm iid}=(2d)^{-d}(d+1)/\bigl[1+(d-1)E_{XY}(d)\bigr]$ with
$E_{XY}(d)=2/3d+(d-1)d_{0}/d$ and $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}\approx1.117$,
the $1.12$ value quoted as the collision-allowed alternative. ∎

1.text:
The $d+1$ point set is ${\cal S}_{d}=\{0,P_{1},\dots ,P_{d}\}$ and the
cross–polytope is non–degenerate iff the $d$ points lie on $d$
different orthogonal axes.  With the usual distinct–axis, one-point-per-
fixed-axis normalisation

$$
P_{i}=U_{i}e_{i},\qquad U_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}{\rm U}(-1,1),
\qquad 1\le i\le d,
$$

a.s.

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}{\cal S}_{d}\bigr)=\frac{|\det [P_{1}\dots P_{d}]|}
{d!}=\frac{|U_{1}\cdots U_{d}|}{d!},
$$

so that with $m_{1}=E|U|=1/2$

$$
V_{d}:=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{m_{1}^{\,d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\qquad V_{1}=1/2 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
d_{0}:=E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
   =E\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}\approx0.765195716,
$$
$E\|0-P_{i}\|=m_{1}$ and on the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs

$$
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\,m_{1}+\binom d2 d_{0}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)d_{0}}{d+1},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Hence on the $E{\rm Vol}/E{\rm dist}$ normalisation

$$
R_{d}^{0}:=\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
       =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)d_{0}},\qquad R_{1}^{0}=1,
$$

$$
R_{2}^{0}= \frac{3}{4\cdot2}\frac1{1+d_{0}}\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}^{0}\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{0}\approx0.00395,\;
R_{5}^{0}\approx0.00038,\dots
$$

$R_{d}^{0}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$.  The series is therefore essentially $R_{1}+R_{2}$,

$$
S_{\infty}^{0}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+ \cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

i.e. $1.250$ on three figures, $R_{1}=1$ and $R_{2}\approx0.212$ providing
essentially the whole remainder.  With the stochastic–stochastic
normalisation $\sum_{d}2^{-d}/(d!d_{0})=(e^{1/2}-1)/d_{0}\approx0.848$.

This is the non-colliding one-per-fixed-axis, distinct mutually orthogonal
segment, cross-polytope reading which is the conventional reading of
“$d$ distinct orthogonal segments and $d$ points”.  The literal
i.i.d. uniform-on-$L_{d}=\bigcup_{i}[-1,1]e_{i}$ reading
$X_{k}=R_{k}e_{I_{k}}$ gives $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$\bar E(d)=[1+(d-1)E_{XY}(d)]/(d+1)$ with
$E_{XY}(d)=2/(3d)+(d-1)d_{0}/d$ and
$R_{d}^{{\rm iid}}=(2d)^{-d}(d+1)/[1+(d-1)E_{XY}(d)]$,
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.109$, $S_{\infty}^{{\rm iid}}\approx1.117$,
the $d!/d^{d}$ permutation factor being precisely the zero-volume
collision event excluded by the distinct-axis requirement. ∎

5.text:
With the wording `distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments' and
`number of points = number of segments = dim' the admissible realisation is
one point per fixed axis.  Put

${\cal S}_{n}=\{0,P_{1},\dots ,P_{n}\},\qquad P_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$,
$U_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}U(-1,1)$,
so that a.s.

${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm co}{\cal S}_{n}\bigr)
 =\dfrac{|U_{1}\cdots U_{n}|}{n!}$,

$V_{n}:=E{\rm Vol}_{n}=m_{1}^{n}/n!$, $m_{1}=E|U|=1/2$,
$V_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$, $V_{1}=1/2$.

For $i\ne j$

$d_{0}:=E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|=E\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}\approx0.765195716$,

$E\|0-P_{i}\|=m_{1}$.  On the $\binom{n+1}{2}$ unordered pairs

$\bar D_{n}
   =\frac{n m_{1}+\binom n2d_{0}}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(n-1)d_{0}}{n+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,$

and on the $E{\rm Vol}/E{\rm dist}$ normalisation

$R_{n}^{0}:=\dfrac{V_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
      =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\,\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)d_{0}},\qquad R_{1}^{0}=1,$

$R_{2}^{0}= \dfrac{3}{8\bigl(1+d_{0}\bigr)}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{0}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{0}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}^{0}\approx0.00038$,

$R_{n}^{0}=O\!\left(2^{-n}/n!\right)$.

Hence

$S_{\infty}^{0}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{0}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

on three figures, the $n=1$ and $n=2$ terms essentially exhausting the
remainder.  With the stochastic–stochastic normalisation
$\sum_{n}2^{-n}/(n!d_{0})=(e^{1/2}-1)/d_{0}\approx0.848$.

This is the non-colliding one-point-per-fixed-axis, i.e. distinct-segment,
cross-polytope model that the statement `distinct mutually orthogonal
segments' and `points = segments' is intended to enforce.  The
$P_{n}=n!/n^{n}$ permutation factor and the $(2n)^{-n}$ volume are the
literal i.i.d. uniform-on-$L_{n}=\bigcup_{i}[-1,1]e_{i}$ reading
$X_{k}=R_{k}e_{I_{k}}$ with axis collisions allowed, which gives
$R_{n}^{\rm iid}=(2n)^{-n}(n+1)/\!\bigl[1+(n-1)E_{XY}(n)\bigr]$,
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$ and $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}\approx1.117$,
the $1.117\approx1.12$ collision value quoted by Colleague 1.  The
$1.250$ distinct-axis value is the conventional cross-polytope reading. ∎

2.text:
With the wording `` $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ and
‘‘ the number of points and line segments matches the dimension ’’ the
admissible $d+1$ point set is the conventional non-colliding
cross-polytope

$${\cal S}_{d}=\{0,P_{1},\dots ,P_{d}\},\qquad 
P_{i}=U_{i}e_{i},\;U_{i}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}{\rm U}(-1,1), $$

a.s. 

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}{\cal S}_{d}\bigr)
   =\frac{|\det [P_{1}\dots P_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\frac{|U_{1}\cdots U_{d}|}{d!},$$

so that with $m_{1}=E|U|=1/2$

$$
V_{d}:=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{m_{1}^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
V_{1}=1/2 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
d_{0}:=E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
     =E\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}\approx0.765195716,
$$

$E\|0-P_{i}\|=m_{1}$ and on the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs

$$
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\,m_{1}+\binom d2d_{0}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)d_{0}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

is the mean pairwise Euclidean distance in ${\cal S}_{d}$.  Hence on the
$E\,{\rm Vol}/E\,{\rm dist}$ normalisation

$$
R_{d}^{A}:=\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
       =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)d_{0}},\qquad R_{1}^{A}=1,
$$

i.e.

* $R_{1}^{A}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}^{A}= \dfrac{3}{2^{2}2!\,[1+d_{0}]}\approx0.21244$
* $R_{3}^{A}\approx0.03293$
* $R_{4}^{A}\approx0.00395$
* $R_{5}^{A}\approx0.00038$

and $R_{d}^{A}=O\!\left(2^{-d}/d!\right)$.  The series is essentially
$R_{1}+R_{2}$,

$$
S^{A}_{\infty}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{A}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

the $d_{0}$-normalised value being $\sum_{d}2^{-d}/(d!d_{0})
=(e^{1/2}-1)/d_{0}\approx0.848$.  This is the distinct-axis,
non-colliding one-point-per-fixed-axis cross-polytope reading enforced
by the distinct-segment requirement.  The $P_{d}=d!/d^{d}$ permutation
factor of the literal i.i.d. uniform on $L_{d}=\cup_{i}[-1,1]e_{i}$
disappears once the zero-volume collision events are removed, which is
the reading intended by the statement.  The literal i.i.d. on the union
reading gives $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and $S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}\simeq
1.117$, the familiar $1.12$ collision model.

d_{0}:=E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
   =E\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv

$$
$E\|0-P_{i}\|=m_{1}$ and on the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs

$$

   =\frac{d\,m_{1}+\binom d2 d_{0}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)d_{0}}{d+1},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2 .

$$

       =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)d_{0}},\qquad R_{1}^{0}=1,
$$

$$
R_{2}^{0}= \frac{3}{4\cdot2}\frac1{1+d_{0}}\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}^{0}\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{0}\approx0.00395,\;
R_{5}^{0}\approx0.00038,\dots
$$

$R_{d}^{0}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$.  The series is therefore essentially $R_{1}+R_{2}$,

$$
S_{\infty}^{0}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+ \cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

i.e. $1.250$ on three figures, $R_{1}=1$ and $R_{2}\approx0.212$ providing
essentially the whole remainder.  With the stochastic–stochastic
normalisation $\sum_{d}2^{-d}/(d!d_{0})=(e^{1/2}-1)/d_{0}\approx0.848$.

segment, cross-polytope reading which is the conventional reading of

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The wording of the query is decisive: the explicit insistence on “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” together with the clause that the number of points equals the number of segments (hence equals dimension) excludes every sampling law that permits axis collisions. Once those measure-zero but volume-destroying events are removed, the admissible realisations reduce exactly to the deterministic one-point-per-fixed-axis construction. The resulting volume expectation is therefore precisely \(2^{-d}/d!\) and the pairwise-distance normaliser is \([1+(d-1)d_0]/(d+1)\).  

The tabulated ratios \(R_1=1\), \(R_2\approx0.21244\), \(R_3\approx0.03293\), … therefore constitute the only series consistent with the geometric constraints. Their sum converges to 1.250 on three decimal places, with the first two terms already supplying more than 96 percent of the total. Any hybrid construction that retains a positive probability of index collisions necessarily violates the orthogonality requirement and must be discarded. The literal i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union model, which yields the 1.117 figure, is thereby ruled out by the problem statement itself. Consensus on the conventional cross-polytope reading now appears unanimous across all five colleagues; further refinement of the numerical value is unnecessary.

With the wording `distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’ and
‘the number of points and line segments matches the dimension’ the only
admissible realisation is the non-colliding one point per fixed axis
cross-polytope

${\cal S}_{d}=\{0,P_{1},\dots ,P_{d}\},\qquad P_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$,
$U_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}{\rm U}(-1,1)$,

a.s.

${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}{\cal S}_{d}\bigr)=|\det[P_{1}\dots P_{d}]|/d!
      =|U_{1}\cdots U_{d}|/d! $

so that with $m_{1}=E|U|=1/2$

$V_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}=m_{1}^{d}/d!=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad V_{1}=1/2$.

For $i\ne j$

$d_{0}=E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|=E\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}\approx0.765195716,$

$E\|0-P_{i}\|=m_{1}$. On the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\,m_{1}+\binom d2 d_{0}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)d_{0}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2.$

Hence on the $E{\rm Vol}/E{\rm dist}$ normalisation

$R_{d}^{0}:=\dfrac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
       =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{\,1+(d-1)d_{0}\,},\qquad R_{1}^{0}=1,$

$R_{2}^{0}= \frac{3}{8\,(1+d_{0})}\approx0.21244,$
$R_{3}^{0}\approx0.03293,$
$R_{4}^{0}\approx0.00395,$
$R_{5}^{0}\approx0.00038,\ldots$

$R_{d}^{0}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$. The series is essentially $R_{1}+R_{2}$,

$S_{\infty}^{0}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

on three figures, $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.212$ providing the whole
remainder. With the stochastic–stochastic normalisation
$\sum_{d}2^{-d}/(d!d_{0})=(e^{1/2}-1)/d_{0}\approx0.848$.

This is the conventional distinct-segment, one-point-per-fixed-axis
cross-polytope reading. The literal i.i.d. uniform-on-$L_{d}
=\cup_{i}[-1,1]e_{i}$ reading $X_{k}=R_{k}e_{I_{k}}$ with axis collisions
allowed gives $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$, $E_{XY}(d)=2/(3d)+(d-1)d_{0}/d$,
